title: Slicing localization: R⌞B_r(x₀) is integer multiplicity with finite mass and boundary mass, and its boundary agrees with ∂R inside B_r(x₀)
statement: Assume (REP), (IMC)(b), (IMC)(d) and (SL), which appear verbatim, in this order, as the hypotheses of the Lean statement. They are the exact frozen statements of cmc_exists_massRepresentation, the second and fourth conjuncts of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, and cmc_slice_mass_bounds. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a representation (μ, ξ) with μ finite on compact subsets of U, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ (plus further properties not used here). (IMC)(b) for an IMRep (M, θ, ξ) of U and a measurable E there is an IMRep of U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. (IMC)(d) the orientation of an IMRep satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x. (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) represented by (μ, ξ) with ∂X represented by (μ', ξ') gives A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' in U, with ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η misses {f = t}, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W (and a pointwise liminf bound not used here). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) integer multiplicity with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and x₀ ∈ U. Then there are r > 0 with closedBall(x₀, r) ⊆ U, a current R' ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) and an IMRep R'' of U representing R' with carrier ⊆ B_r(x₀), such that M(R') < ∞, M(∂R') < ∞ (M = mass in U), and ∂R'(η) = ∂R(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀).
